newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFIs to pay tax on gains from selling firms.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFIs to pay tax on gains from selling firms.

text.p: Poland's finance ministry will scrap next year the corporate tax exemption which the National Investment Funds (NFI) enjoy on gains from selling firms from their portfolios, a ministry official said on Friday.
"As of 1998, revenues from sales of shares of companies that were allocated to NFI will be taxed," Stanislaw Dzierzyc from the ministry's direct taxation department told Reuters.
Poland's 38 percent corporate tax will be lowered to 36 percent next year.
Under Poland's mass privatisation programme, 15 NFIs were given control last year of over 60-percent stakes in more than 500 medium-size companies.
Each fund, run by international consortia of managers, was given a leading, 33-percent stake in more than 30 companies and small equities in the remaining firms.
Some funds said the ministry's decision would make them less attractive to investors.

"We will not be able to convince investors that the return on shares will cover the cost of their buying. Here I also mean the tax on sales of selling firms," said Piotr Rymaszewski, president of the Octava fund.
But some others saw no radical change stemming from the regulations.
Yamaichi Regent Special, the firm running the Fortuna NFI, said the introduction of the tax would not change his fund's portfolio management strategy.
Shares in NFIs are to enter the Warsaw stock exchange in mid-year. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
